title: GPT for RCTs? Using AI to determine adherence to clinical trial reporting guidelines

paper.repo: https://osf.io/4shmt (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/4SHMT) - OSF project 'GPT_4_RCT' ('Using AI to examine RCT data'), public, created 2023-08-16, modified 2025-02-27; child components 'Data' (osf.io/htvmk) and 'manscript' (osf.io/tyx5s)
paper.repo_note: OSF 'Data' component (osf.io/htvmk, osfstorage) verified 2026-09-04: pmid_list.csv (1,022 B), image_details.csv (2,208 B), scripts_for_extraction/ (1_pmcdata.Rmd, 2_epubdata.Rmd, 3_pdfdata.Rmd, 4_joindata.Rmd, Readme.txt), analysis/ (15 files: per-item CSVs outcome.csv, hypothesis.csv, person_conceal.csv, eligibility.csv, sample_size.csv, rand_technique.csv, rand_method.csv, effect.csv, blind.csv, Llama2.csv, image_details.csv - each ~5-7 KB, i.e. per-paper labels/results, not article text; 1. GPT_4_training.Rmd, 2. GPT_4_testing.Rmd, 3.Llama_testing.Rmd, gpt_4functions.R), pilot/scripts_for_analysis/. The 'manscript' component (osf.io/tyx5s) listing timed out. The paper also promises the MI-CLAIM checklist and raw label-transformation spreadsheets.

dependence.note: The LLM is the classifier whose YES/NO adherence judgments are scored against human labels (Schulz et al. 2022); the paper's primary outcome (F1) is entirely a property of GPT-4 Turbo's outputs.

claim.statement: GPT-4 Turbo (temperature 0.2, top-p 0.2, persona system prompt + per-item task/question user prompts) determined CONSORT-item adherence in the TEST split (20% of ~982 text-question pairs from 113 sports-medicine RCT reports) with pooled F1 = 0.89 and accuracy 90% (95% CI 85-94%); per-item accuracy ranged 83-100% (Table 2, Figure 1).
claim.metric: F1 (primary) and classification accuracy with 95% CI of YES/NO adherence answers vs. Schulz et al. labels, pooled over 9 text items in the TEST split
claim.original_source: Abstract; Results 'GPT-4 performance'; Table 2 (F1 and accuracy per item); Figure 1 (confusion matrix); Table 1 (pair counts and adherence rates)

protocol.model_note: Analysis ran alongside 'GPT-4 Vision' (gpt-4-vision-preview era), submitted 2024-05-14, so the snapshot was most likely gpt-4-1106-preview or gpt-4-0125-preview (both dead 2026-03-26). gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (GA 2024-04-09, vision built in) is the only live candidate and cannot be confirmed.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions ('chat' format; images as base64 for the vision items)
protocol.prompt_source: System prompt verbatim in Methods 'Model choice and optimisation' ('You are a health researcher reviewing a scientific article for a peer-reviewed sports medicine journal ... Step 1: Summarize ... Step 2: Answer the question with either YES or NO only.'); user prompts (Task + Question per item) in online supplemental table S2 (example for item 1 verbatim in the paper); prompts were iteratively rewritten with ChatGPT on TRAIN errors

params.max_tokens: 'The model response was limited to 512 tokens' (Data extraction section)
params.other: input = one paper section (introduction / method / results; methods+results for item 9) + task + question; Llama 2 comparator on TogetherAI with temperature/top-p 0.7

protocol.n_items_note: TEST split = 20% of 982 pairs, stratified by section; exact count in online supplemental table S1 / OSF
protocol.evaluation: Parse the Step-2 'YES'/'NO' and compare with the Schulz et al. label; F1 and accuracy (with 95% CI) pooled over items - automatic given labels and split membership

budget.assumptions: TEST split only: ~196 pairs x 3 seeds; ~2,500 input tokens (paper section + prompts) and ~250 output tokens (summary + YES/NO). Running all 982 pairs would be ~USD 96.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1: survival if pooled TEST accuracy has a Wilson 95% CI (n~196) overlapping 0.90 [0.85-0.94] and pooled F1 >= 0.85; direction: >= 80% accuracy on every text item (the paper's 'acceptable performance' claim). The Llama-2 fine-tuning comparison is not re-run.
judgment.notes: Class imbalance matters (item 9: 20% adherence -> F1 0.57 at 87% accuracy); report per-item F1 alongside accuracy.

domain_notes: Ground truth is Schulz et al.'s (2022) audit of CONSORT reporting in 160 sports-medicine trials published in 2020 - a human judgment with its own subjectivity, so 'accuracy' is agreement with one audit. Papers were split into introduction/method/results sections to fit Llama 2's context window; item 9 (effect size + CI) used methods+results and was excluded from Llama 2. Figure 1's confusion-matrix axes are labelled unusually (actual = model output, predicted = Schulz labels).
